lede: Israel's president has picked Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, to try to form the next government, after 67 of 120 MPs backed him.
Qatar is still shuttling a draft deal between Washington and Tehran, and US, Russian and Ukrainian delegations are due in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.
At home, new polling has One Nation in front and Angus Taylor narrowly ahead of Anthony Albanese as preferred prime minister, with CBA's trading update on Wednesday the next test for the banks.

stories.h: Herzog picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to try to form Israel's next government
stories.b: President Isaac Herzog said parties holding 67 of the 120 Knesset seats recommended Eisenkot, against 46 for Netanyahu. Eisenkot is due to be formally handed the mandate on Sunday and has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible 14 day extension. Arab parties endorsed him but have not said they will join his government, and the ultra Orthodox UTJ party backed neither man.
stories.w: Eisenkot probably cannot reach 61 seats without Arab party support, and some of his own allies reject that. This shapes Israel's war strategy, the Iran talks and its ties with Washington.

stories.h: Qatar's draft US and Iran deal moves on, but Tehran keeps its conditions
stories.b: Qatar says both sides are reviewing a draft to end the war, and one report says the US has approved the memorandum Qatari mediators presented to Iran. Versions described in the press start with a few days of confidence building steps, including the US lifting its naval blockade and releasing part of Iran's frozen funds, with Iran allowing nuclear inspectors in and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran says Hormuz opens only once the US meets its seven conditions. The reports rely on unnamed sources.
stories.w: About a fifth of the world's oil normally moves through Hormuz, so a deal or a collapse feeds straight into fuel prices and Australian inflation.

stories.h: US to host Russia and Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November
stories.b: Envoy Steve Witkoff announced a new round with Ukrainian and Russian delegations. His agenda lists post war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian measures. Russia wants Ukraine to hand over the roughly 20 percent of the Donbas it does not yet control, and Zelensky has rejected limits on Ukraine's military.
stories.w: The talks are not a leaders' summit, so a settlement this week is unlikely. The result still affects European security, energy prices and sanctions.

quick.x: Reports differ on how long Eisenkot's mandate runs, with CNN saying up to six weeks and others saying 28 days plus a 14 day extension.
Eisenkot is said to be holding to mandatory military service for ultra Orthodox men even as Avigdor Liberman opens the door to their parties.

stories.h: OpenAI reportedly raises about $11 billion, well short of its $30 billion target
stories.b: Reports citing the Wall Street Journal say OpenAI has around $11 billion committed in a round once meant to raise $30 billion, at a valuation of about $1.25 trillion. It has reportedly cut its valuation goal from $1.4 trillion and plans to chase family offices and wealthy individuals for up to $20 billion more. OpenAI declined to comment and terms are still being negotiated, so the numbers could change.
stories.w: It is a sign investors are getting choosier about AI spending after a rough week for chip stocks, which matters for super funds and ETFs holding big tech.

stories.h: Big tech's AI spending is estimated at $766 billion this year, while their value has fallen
stories.b: One estimate puts the 2026 AI spending of seven large US tech firms at about $766 billion. The same report says their combined market value is down roughly $4.85 trillion from 2026 peaks. This comes from a secondary outlet, so treat the figures as estimates.
stories.w: The gap between huge spending and falling share prices is why Nvidia's results on 17 November are being watched so closely.

quick.x: Wall Street's Nasdaq rose about 1.1% on Friday after a bruising week for AI stocks, and investors lifted bets on a Fed rate cut in December.
Morningstar says Nvidia fell 9% on Thursday, its worst day since January 2025, before bouncing on Friday.

stories.h: New poll has One Nation first and Angus Taylor narrowly ahead as preferred PM
stories.b: A YouGov poll for News24 Pulse put One Nation first on primary vote, with Labor and the Coalition behind it. Taylor leads Albanese as preferred prime minister 41 to 39. Earlier Newspolls this year also had One Nation level with or ahead of Labor, though I could not find a fresh November Newspoll to compare.
stories.w: Voters are punishing both major parties over cost of living and rates. A three way split makes preference flows decisive at the next federal election.

stories.h: Albanese defends his Caribbean trip as the Coalition says he should have stayed home
stories.b: The Prime Minister attended the Commonwealth leaders' meeting in Antigua and Barbuda from 31 October to 4 November, the first Australian PM visit to the Caribbean since 2009. He was away when the RBA lifted rates, which the opposition seized on. He argued the trip helps unite middle powers and diversify trade, and more summits in Turkey, the Philippines, China and the US are coming.
stories.w: With rates up and polls sliding, travel is now a political line of attack, and the government is under pressure to show a cost of living plan.

quick.x: Taylor says the Prime Minister and Treasurer are in denial about the economy after the RBA rate rise.

stories.h: CBA's first quarter update on Wednesday is the first bank read since the rate rise
stories.b: Commonwealth Bank releases a short trading update for the first quarter of FY27 on 11 November. It is not a full result: CBA only updates in the first and third quarters. Its last full year result showed cash profit of about $10.98 billion, a net interest margin of 2.05% and a 12.0% CET1 capital ratio.
stories.w: Investors will look for signs of mortgage margins, bad debts and customer stress after the cash rate hit 4.85%.

stories.h: Share market closed higher on the day of the 'no surprise' RBA hike
stories.b: The ASX 200 added about 30 points, or 0.3%, to close at 8,887 on Tuesday 3 November. The RBA lifted the cash rate 25 basis points to 4.85%, and the Australian dollar eased to about 69.79 US cents from 70.21. Markets had largely priced the rise in.
stories.w: A move that is already priced in rarely shocks markets, but higher rates keep squeezing mortgage holders and the housing market.

quick.x: ANZ said in August that the value of its home loan applications fell 12% after the May Budget property tax changes.

explainer.body: A minority government is one whose party or alliance holds fewer than half the seats in parliament. To pass laws and survive confidence votes it needs help from outside parties, who may back it without taking cabinet jobs. That is called external support. Eisenkot could end up in this position in Israel if Arab parties back him from outside the coalition. Australia has seen it too, as when Julia Gillard relied on independents and the Greens after 2010.
